That:

That Council:
  1. Make an area adjacent to the Cross Strip available for Licence to Textron Systems Australia Pty Ltd, for a Flight Operations Site  subject to the lodgement and approval of a Development Application and the applicant meeting all costs associated with the development;
  2. The development to include an all weather access road and new security gates at the access point;
  3.   5. The annual licence fee be set at $1580.00 per annum (including GST) and the Licence fee be subject to annual 3% increases; and
  6. The licence agreement be subject to any terms and conditions as negotiated by Council’s General Manager.

Carried

RESOLUTION 2025/74  
Moved:  Cr Joanne Williams
Seconded:  Cr Fiona Brown

That:

1. The following works be funded from the Urban Works Vote and be included in the 2025/2026 Budget:

i. Inverell and Villages - Urban Renewal and Upgrade General Fund, Water Fund

2. That:
i. The budget allocations of $2.995M for the 2025/2026 ACRD Program be endorsed and a further report be presented to Council in respect of the funding allocations and individual works proposed to be undertaken under this program; 

ii. The budget allocation of $160K for the RMS Supplementary Block Grant Program be the subject of a further report to Council;

iii. The budget allocation of $3.157M for the 2025/2026 Block Grant Program be endorsed and a further report be presented to Council in respect of the specific projects to be funded;

iv. The budget allocation of $2.468M for the 2025/2026 Roads to Recovery Program be endorsed and a further report be presented to Council in respect of the specific projects to be funded; and

v. The budget allocation of $544.99K for the RERRF/REPAIR Program be endorsed and a report on the projects for the RERRF / REPAIR Program for 2025/2026 be presented to Council in respect of the specific projects to be funded.  

3. That Council utilises the maximum permissible rate increase allowed by IPART of 4.0%.

4. That:

i. Council provide an allocation of $110K for joint industry promotions and assistance;

ii. The 2025/2026 Strategic Capital Infrastructure Fund of $670K be utilised for loan repayments for the Inverell Aquatic Centre Redevelopment;

iii. Additional interest on investments of $446K be allocated to Strategic Capital Infrastructure Fund to fund future capital projects;

iv. The budget allocation of $324K for the 2025/2026 Special Projects - Roads Infrastructure Fund be endorsed;

v. The transfers to and from Internally Restricted Assets be endorsed; and

vi. The list of additional one-off budget adjustments listed in section 5.2.2 & 5.2.3 of the report be endorsed.

5. That:
i. The following rating categories be utilised for the 2025/2026 rating year:        
       Residential - Inverell
            Residential - General 
            Residential - Ashford
            Residential - Delungra
            Residential - Gilgai
            Residential - Yetman
            Residential - Tingha
            Residential - Rural 
            Business - Inverell Industrial / Commercial 
            Business - Other
            Farmland
            Mining

ii. A General Base Amount of $235 plus an Ad Valorem Rate be determined for the categories detailed above.

6. That the Interest Rate applicable to Outstanding Rates and Charges for 2025/2026 be the maximum allowable as advised by the Office of Local Government of 10.5%.

7. That the following Waste Management Charges be adopted:

8. That the Fees and Charges, as recommended, be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.

9. That:
  1. the Stormwater Management Service Charge be set at the maximum amount allowable of $25.00 per Residential Premises, $12.50 per Residential Strata lot, and $25.00 for Business Premises for each 350 square metres or additional part thereof, subject to a maximum charge on Business Premises of $200.00; and

  2. the Stormwater Management Program as recommended being Gilgai Drainage Project as per the adopted Gilgai Drainage Plan, be adopted.  

10. That the proposed capital expenditure program for 2025/2026 be adopted.

11. That:
i. the report on the 2025/2026 budget be noted;
ii. the draft estimates (incorporating the Operational Plan and Long Term Financial Plan) for the General Activities for 2025/2026 be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.

12. That:
  1. the Sewerage Charges as listed below be adopted for 2025/2026.


  2. The Draft Estimates (incorporating Operational Plan) for the Sewerage Fund for 2025/2026 be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.

13. That:
  1. the 2025/2026 "Deficit Budget" of $80K for the Water Fund, before Grants and Contributions provided for Capital Purposes be adopted;
  2. the Water Charges as listed below be adopted for 2025/2026.

  3. the draft Estimates (incorporating Operational Plan) for the Water Fund for 2025/2026 be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.  

Carried

RESOLUTION  2025/171
Moved:  Cr Joanne Williams
Seconded:  Cr Wendy Wilks

That Council:
  1. Pursuant to section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993, adopt the 2025/2026 Operational Plan and Budget (including the Statement of Revenue Policy) as per Attachment 1. 

  2. Pursuant to clause 211(2) of the Local Government General Regulation 2021, approve expenditure and vote funds as detailed in the 2025/2026 Operational Plan and Budget. 

  3. Pursuant to section 403 of the Local Government Act 1993, adopt the 2025/2035 Long Term Financial Plan forming part of Council's Resourcing Strategy as per Attachment 2.

  4. Pursuant to section 608 of the Local Government Act 1993, adopt the 2025/2026 Fees and Charges as per Attachment 3.

  5. In accordance with Chapter 15, Parts 4 and 5 of the Local Government Act 1993, make and levy the following rates and annual charges for the 01 July 2025 to 30 June 2026 (2025-2026 financial year):
  1.  Ordinary Rates pursuant to section 494 of the Local Government Act 1993:

    1. Residential Inverell: A rate of 1.02277 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable residential land in the town of Inverell;
    2. Residential Ashford.  A rate of 1.00795 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable residential land in the village of Ashford;
    3. Residential Delungra. A rate of 1.42350 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable residential land in the village of Delungra;
    4. Residential Gilgai - A rate of 0.79185 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable residential land in the village of Gilgai;
    5. Residential Yetman.  A rate of 1.95660 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable residential land in the village of Yetman;
    6. Residential Tingha.  A rate of 4.69400 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable residential land in the village of Tingha;
    7. Residential Rural. A rate of 0.38140 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable land that satisfies the description of Rural Residential land as defined by the Local Government Act 1993;
    8. Residential General.  A rate of 0.55100 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all other rateable residential land not declared within one of the other Residential sub-categories.
    9. Farmland.  A rate of 0.18586 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all rateable land in the Shire being farmland;
    10. Business Inverell. A rate of 2.86720 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all non-residential land within the town of Inverell;
    11. Business Other.  A rate of 2.04639 in the dollar on the 2024 land value of all other business land in the Shire;
    12. Mining.  A rate of 11.5 cents in the dollar on the 2024 land value for all rateable land that satisfies the description of Mining land as defined by the Local Government Act 1993;
    13. The Base Amount for each rateable assessment be $235.00 for all categories and sub-categories.



  2. Annual Water Charges pursuant to Section 501, 502 and 552 Local Government Act 1993:



  3. Water Usage Charges pursuant to Section 552 Local Government Act 1993:


  4. Sewerage Charges pursuant to Section 501, 502 and 552 Local Government Act 1993:

  5. Waste Management Charge pursuant to Section 501 Local Government Act 1993:



  6. Domestic Waste Management Charge pursuant to Section 496 Local Government Act 1993:


  7. Waste Management Charge (Commercial) pursuant to Section 502 Local Government Act 1993:


  8. Stormwater Management Service Charge pursuant to Section 496A Local Government Act 1993:


  1. Pursuant to section 566(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, adopt the overdue rates and charges at the maximum interest rate of 10.5 per cent for the period 01 July 2025 to 30 June 2026 in accordance with the determination made by the Minister for Local Government as published in the NSW Government Gazette.

Carried

That:

  1. Council notes the many concerns expressed by adjoining landholders and others at the planned development of the Inverell Battery Energy Storage System at 6219 Gwydir Highway, Inverell;

  3.   5. Council commits to providing via social media and other means any updated information relevant to the scoping study and planning process.
Carried

RESOLUTION  2025/267
Moved:  Cr Jo Williams
Seconded:  Cr Wendy Wilks

That:
  1. the report be received and noted;
  2. Council's DRAFT 2024/2025 Financial Statements be "referred to audit" in accordance with s413(1) of the Local Government Act 1993;
  3. if during the audit process, the NSW Audit Office requires any material changes, or discovers any audit issues that would render the Financial Statements false or misleading in any way, the draft financial statements are to be returned to Council for further consideration;
  4. Council record as an opinion of Council, in accordance with s413(2c) of the Local Government Act 1993, that the draft 2024/2025 annual financial report is in accordance with:
  • the Local Government Act 1993 (as amended) and the Regulations made thereunder;
  • the Australian Accounting Standards and professional pronouncements; 
  • the Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting; 
  • presents fairly the Council’s operating result and financial position for the year;
  • accords with Council’s accounting and other records; and
  • that the Council is not aware of any matter that would render this report false or misleading in any way.
  1. subject to no material audit changes or audit issues discovered as a result of the audit process:
  1. the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, General Manager and Responsible Accounting Officer be authorised to sign the statements as required by s413(2) of the Local Government Act 1993;
  1. Council authorise the General Manager to forward the Financial Statements to the Office of Local Government upon receipt of the Audit Reports from the NSW Audit Office;
  1. Council authorise the General Manager to place the audited Financial Statements on public exhibition and provide notice in accordance with s418(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, that Council will consider the Reports of its Auditors for the year ended 30 June 2025 at its November Ordinary Meeting; and 
  1. Council present the signed audited Financial Statements to the public at the November Ordinary Council Meeting in accordance with s419(1) Local Government Act 1993.


Carried

That Inverell Shire Council submit the following motion to the 2025 Annual Local Government NSW Conference:

'That Local Government NSW call on the Minister for Local Government to review and amend the current Local Government Investment Order (2011) to broaden the range of authorised investments available to councils by:

  1. Reinstating the ability to invest in securities with recognised investment-grade credit ratings (e.g. Moody’s ≥A2, S&P ≥A, Fitch ≥A), as permitted under the 2005 Investment Order; and
  2. Expanding the Investment Order to allow councils to prudently invest in additional regulated asset classes, including:
  • Direct property investments (income-producing commercial, industrial, or mixed-use assets),
  • Australian Real Estate Investment Trusts (A-REITs),
  • Diversified managed funds (fixed income, infrastructure and balanced funds),
  • Corporate securities which are senior-ranked (Bonds & Floating Rate Notes (FRNs)), with a minimum long-term credit rating of A'.
Carried

ENTITLEMENT		PREVIOUS DELEGATES
Aboriginal Consultative Committee
Established to promote an increased knowledge and understanding of Aboriginal Culture and society in the wider community and to develop the interests of the Aboriginal people in the local area. 
 		Mayor, General Manager, 1 Ashford Local Land Council,
1 Anaiwan Local Land Council,
5 members of the community
  • Mayor

Committee established to guide the internal audit function of Council. 		1 Representative (excluding the Mayor), and 3 independents
  • Cr Williams
Conduct Review Committee (Statutory term)
Committee that establishes the facts of an allegation that has been referred to it in accordance with the provisions of Council’s Code of Conduct.		1 Representative
(Mayor), General Manager), and 3 independents
  • Mayor

Local Emergency Management Committee (LEMC)
- Provision of the State Emergency Rescue and Management Act. The role of the LEMC is to:
  • Prevent or reduce the impact of emergencies;
  • Ensure the preparedness of our community;
  • Provide an effective and coordinated response to the emergency;
  • Provide for the recovery of our community.
 		Local Emergency Management Officer (LEMO) 
  • Chairperson - Director Civil Services 
  • Manager Civil Engineering (LEMO).
 
 
 
Inverell Local Transport Forum (ILTF)
A technical review committee that advises the Council on matters for which the Council has delegated authority.
Council is not bound by the advice given by the ILTF, however if Council does wish to act contrary to the unanimous advice of the ILTF or when the advice is not unanimous, it must notify the RMS & the NSW Police before proceeding.		ILTF comprises 4 formal representatives:
- 1 Council
- 1 NSW Police
- 1 RMS
- 1 Local State Member or their nominee
  • Director Civil Services (delegated by the General Manager)
 
Waste Management Sunset Committee
A Committee formed to: 
  1. Review the approved Waste Management Strategy and recommend any appropriate amendments to Council for consideration, and
  2. The issues of Container Deposit Scheme and scavenging rights be referred to the Sunset Committee for consideration.
Director Environmental Services and 3 Representatives 
  • Cr Ross
  • Cr King
  • Cr Kachel
  • Director Environmental Services

Item: Sale of Land - Rifle Range Road Industrial Subdivision 

Description: Council is in receipt of correspondence requesting to withdraw from the purchase of Lot 8 DP 1286921 Sierra Drive Inverell and making a new offer for Lot 4 DP 1286921 Sierra Drive Inverell. Council is being asked to make a determination in respect of the withdrawal and new offer.

COMMENTARY:

In accordance with the provisions of Section 9 (2A) Local Government Act 1993, the General Manager is of the opinion that consideration of the following item(s) is likely to take place when the meeting is closed to the public.

Item: General Manager Annual Performance Review for 2024/2025.

Description: This report outlines the results of the General Manager’s Annual Review of performance conducted by the Council’s Performance Review Committee on 11 November 2025. 

Reason: Section 10A (2) (a) Local Government Act 1993 Personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors) .

Item: Request for a Reduction under Council Policy Water Usage Charges - Undetected Leaks.

Description: Council has received a request for a reduction in a water account under Council’s ‘Water Usage Charges – Undetected Leaks Policy’. The request has been received from Ray White Real Estate, the managing agent of 26 Vernon Street, Inverell on behalf of the owner.

Reason: Section 10A (2) (b) Local Government Act 1993 The personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer Local Government Act 1993.

Item: Request for a Reduction under Council Policy Water Usage Charges - Undetected Leaks.

Description: Council has received a request from the property owner of 2 Tulare Crescent, Inverell.  The property owner is seeking Council’s assistance by issuing an amended account based on average usage due to unexplained usage.

Reason: Section 10A (2) (b) Local Government Act 1993 The personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer Local Government Act 1993.

1. It is a condition of a development consent for development that involves building work that the work must be carried out in accordance with the requirements of the Building Code of Australia.
2. It is a condition of a development consent for development that involves residential building work for which a contract of insurance is required under the Home Building Act 1989, Part 6 that a contract of insurance is in force before building work is authorised to be carried out by the consent commences.
3. It is a condition of a development consent for a temporary structure used as an entertainment venue that the temporary structure must comply with Part B1 and NSW Part H102 in Volume 1 of the Building Code of Australia.
4. In subsection (1), a reference to the Building Code of Australia is a reference to the Building Code of Australia as in force on the day on which the application for the construction certificate was made.
5. In subsection (3), a reference to the Building Code of Australia is a reference to the Building Code of Australia as in force on the day on which the application for development consent was made.
6. This section does not apply -  
  1. to the extent to which an exemption from a provision of the Building Code of Australia or a fire safety standard is in force under the Environmental Planning and Assessment (Development Certification and Fire Safety) Regulation 2021, or
  2. to the erection of a temporary building, other than a temporary structure to which subsection (3) applies.

Condition reason: Prescribed condition under section 69 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021.

 2.

Erection of signs 

1. This section applies to a development consent for development involving building work, subdivision work or demolition work.
2. It is a condition of the development consent that a sign must be erected in a prominent position on a site on which building work, subdivision work or demolition work is being carried out -
  1. showing the name, address, and telephone number of the principal certifier for the work, and
  2. showing the name of the principal contractor, if any, for the building work and a telephone number on which the principal contractor may be contacted outside working hours, and
  3. stating that unauthorised entry to the work site is prohibited.
3. The sign must be - 
  1. maintained while the building work, subdivision work or demolition work is being carried out, and
  2. removed when the work has been completed.
4. This section does not apply in relation to - 
  1. building work, subdivision work or demolition work carried out inside an existing building, if the work does not affect the external walls of the building, or
  2. Crown building work certified to comply with the Building Code of Australia under the Act, Part 6.

Condition reason: Prescribed condition under section 70 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021.

3.

Approved plans and supporting documentation 

Development must be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents, except where the conditions of this consent expressly require otherwise.

 4.

Temporary use time limit 

Pursuant to Section 4.17(1)(d) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, this consent is limited to a period of 12 months from the date of commencement of the use.

Notice of the commencement must be provided in writing to Council prior to the use commencing.

Condition reason: To ensure that there is a reasonable time limitation placed on the temporary use. 

 5.

Removal of temporary use additions 

Pursuant to Section 4.17(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, any minor additions (i.e. fencing, signage, speed zones), associated with the temporary use above must be removed at the end of the time period or when the use ceases onsite, whichever is the lesser. The cost of removal of any additions must be borne by the applicant/proponent. 

Condition reason: To remove features not relevant to the site once the temporary use ceases. 

Before issue of an occupation certificate 

6.

Occupation of premises

Prior to occupation of the premises, an Occupation Certificate must be issued in accordance with Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

Note:  Prior to issue of the Occupation Certificate, the Principal Certifying Authority is required to be satisfied, amongst other things, that:

  •  all required inspections (including each applicable mandatory critical stage inspection) have been carried out; and
  • any preconditions to the issue of the certificate required by a development consent have been met.

Condition reason: To ensure an Occupation Certificate is obtained prior to use of the building. 

 7.

Carparking upgrades 

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, the site access and carparking area must be sealed, line marked and provided with adequate internal signage. A carpark line marking layout plan must be submitted to and approved by Council prior to implementation in accordance with Council standards and AS 2890.

Necessary sediment and erosions control measures must be implemented during works. 

Condition reason: To ensure a suitable surface treatment to parking areas, minimise offsite impacts and provide sediment and erosion control during works. 

8.

Section 138 

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, approval under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 is to be obtained for the sealing of the existing access.

Necessary sediment and erosions control measures must be implemented during works.

Condition reason: To ensure all necessary approvals under the Roads Act 1993 are obtained for the development. 

9.

Section 68 

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, approval under Section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993 is to be obtained from Council to undertake upgrade works to the onsite sewerage management system.

Condition reason: To ensure an approval under Local Government Act 1993 is obtained for the development. 

10.

Fire Safety Measures 

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, an Annual Fire Safety Certificate, less than six (6) months old must be submitted to Council.

Condition reason: To ensure that suitable fire safety measures are provided in the event of an emergency. 

11.

Temporary signage

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, details of any signage associated with the temporary use must be submitted to and approved by Council. Alternatively, confirmation by a suitably qualified consultant must be submitted to confirm that the signage complies with exempt development provisions. 

Condition reason: To ensure any temporary signage complies with the relevant planning legislation. 

12.

Temporary fencing

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, a temporary fence must be installed within the boundary of the property to delineate the parking area from the rear yard. The fence must also be setback at least 5m from the property boundary to restrict access around the rear yard (play area). 

Condition reason: To ensure that children's safety is maximised and additional buffer is provided to the residential neighbours from the play area.

13.

School registration

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, the proponent must submit to Council either a copy of the school registration with the Department of Education, or confirmation that a relevant exemption is in place relating to registration of the temporary school.

Condition reason: Ensure that the property and units are suitably identified.

 14.

Waste management

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, the proponent is to provide Council a waste management plan nominating all necessary ongoing waste management practices and details, including but not limited to the type of waste material and method of storage and disposal.

Condition reason: To ensure appropriate ongoing waste management.

15.

School speed zones

Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate, the proponent must liaise with Transport for NSW (TfNSW) to complete a speed zone review for this development. A copy of TfNSW review must be submitted to Council.

The cost to implement and decommission any required speed zone changes are to be borne by the applicant/proponent.

Condition reason: To ensure adequate consultation with Transport for NSW (TfNSW) and implementation of any required school speed zones to enhance safety.

Ongoing use
16.

Hours of operation - standard

The premises is restricted to operate within the hours of Monday to Friday 8.00am to 4.30pm during the NSW school terms.

Condition reason: To ensure hours of operation are in accordance with the approved use.

17.

Amenity and Noise

No external public address system is to be used on-site.

Condition reason: To ensure the amenity of the area is protected

18.

Hours of operation - incidental

The proponent must provide Council with prior notice of any intention to operate the use outside the approved hours above for any incidental purpose, such as for a school disco or other event.

The notice must be in writing and submitted at least two (2) weeks prior to the event. A letter drop to neighbours advising of the incidental additional operation hours must also be completed at least one (1) week prior to the event.

The notice and letter drop must include, at minimum, the event type, date and operating times of the event, as well as the contact details of the relevant school staff member to discuss the event.

Condition reason: To ensure the amenity of the area is protected. 

19.

Vehicle movements 

All vehicles must enter and leave the site in a forward direction.

Condition reason: To ensure the safety and efficiency of Fernhill Road. 

20.

Restriction on site access 

No buses must access the site or stop in the road reserve in front of the site on Fernhill or Yetman Roads.

Condition reason: To ensure safety and efficiency of Fernhill Road and Yetman Road. 

21.

Restriction on student numbers 

 

A maximum of 45 Primary school students and 4 full-time equivalent (FTE) staff are permitted for the development.

 

Condition reason: To limit the scale of the temporary use.

At this juncture, the Mayor acknowledged the tragic events that occurred at Bondi on Sunday, 14 December 2025. The Mayor condemned the attack as an assault on our society and expressed Council’s deepest sympathies to all those impacted.  The Mayor also commended the efforts of health, police, emergency services personnel and anyone else that responded to the incident. Cr Dight acknowledged Waverley Council for its work in managing the ongoing impacts within the community.

Council’s thoughts were extended to the victims, their families, and all those affected by this tragedy. A minute’s silence was then observed.

RESOLUTION  2025/344
Moved:  Cr Greg Kachel

That Council accede to the request and grant the following support for the 2026 Joeys Mini World Cup event: 

  • All field usage charges for the duration of the event - $8,280.00
  • Lighting charges - $400.00 
  • Provide all line marking - $7,500.00
  • Provide toilet facilities and rubbish removal - $2,000.00
  • Provide use of the Clubhouse at no charge - $1,400.00
  • Provide hire of the Town Hall at no charge to conduct the Presentation Night - $775.00
  • The Event Organiser unconditionally indemnify (release) Council from all claims, suits, demands, actions or proceedings (whether at law, in equity or arising under any statute) arising out of or in connection with the conduct of the event
  • The Event Organiser provides a summary of the number and origin of participants/teams including postcodes and country of residence
  • The Event Organiser provides a written report summarising the event and all media coverage within 30 days of conducting the event. Total cost of support $20,355.00.

Carried

RESOLUTION  2025/345
Moved:  Cr Fiona Brown
Seconded:  Cr Ian Hooker

That Council:
  1. Give public notice of the proposed five (5) year licence to Inverell Sporties Ltd for the use of Part Lot 7 DP 1152029 (part Reserve R2156), Glen Innes Road, Inverell, in accordance with Sections 47 and 47A of the Local Government Act 1993;
     
  2. Exhibit the proposal for a minimum period of 28 days, commencing 12 January 2026 and closing at 5:00pm on 9 February 2026, inviting public submissions on the proposed licence agreement.
     
  3. Subject to no submissions being received during the exhibition period, authorise the General Manager to finalise and execute the licence agreement on behalf of Council, with the following terms:

    1. Council renew the agreement with Inverell Sporties Ltd for Part Lot 7 DP 1152029 (part Reserve R2156), Glen Innes Road, Inverell;
    2. the licence agreement be for a five (5) year period;
    3. the licence fee be $3,000 per annum (GST inclusive) with an annual increase of 3%; and
    4. the licence agreement be subject to any other terms and conditions as negotiated by Council’s General Manager.

  4. If any submissions are received during the exhibition period, or if a request is received from the Minister under Section 47A(2)(c), a further report be presented to Council detailing the submissions and/or Ministerial request and recommending a course of action in accordance with Sections 47(3)–(4) and 47A of the Local Government Act 1993.

Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/06
Moved:  Cr Wendy Wilks
Seconded:  Cr Fiona Brown

That Inverell Shire Council submit the following motion to the 2026 National General Assembly:

'Motion - Healthcare Workforce'
This National General Assembly calls on the Australian Government to strengthen healthcare workforce supply, retention and service continuity in regional, rural and remote (RRR) communities by:

  • Establishing more training places and pathways in Rural and Regional areas for advanced skills in Obstetrics, Anaesthetics, Emergency, Aboriginal medicine, surgery, internal medicine, paediatrics and academic medicine.  
  • Where practicable establishing ‘simulation education’ and hybrid training programs via video link or 'hub and spoke' models, providing continuity of training pathways from university, to intern, to junior doctor and then to Rural Generalist. 
  • Create and enhance funding programs to enable medical training students adequate financial support while on rural clinical placement. 
  • Partner with other tiers of government to provide accommodation and support training to 'grow our own' nursing and medical workforce.

Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Mr Justin Pay, Director Civil Services declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 11.2 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay's sister is part owner of the subject property. Please note previous declarations regarding this matter have been made at pre-lodgement stage and submission of DA stage. Mr Pay has taken no part or had no involvement in the assessment of this application.  

Mr Paul Pay, Director Corporate and Community Services declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 11.2 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay is related to the owners of the land who are also the proponents of the DA application.  

Cr Greg Kachel declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 11.2 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'. The nature of the interest is that Cr Kachel has a personal relationship with the owners of the property, to which the DA applies, who are extended family members.

Note: Cr Greg Kachel, Mr Justin Pay (Director Civil Services) and Mr Paul Pay (Director Corporate and Community Services) left the Chamber at 11:16am.







Motion 
Moved:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
Seconded:  Cr Ian Hooker

That Development Application 66/2025 for the Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999-head feedlot and associated infrastructure at 2321 Ashford Road, Bukkulla be approved subject to the following conditions of consent:

General Conditions 

1.

Compliance with Building Code of Australia and insurance requirements under Home Building Act 1989 

  1. It is a condition of a development consent for development that involves building work that the work must be carried out in accordance with the requirements of the Building Code of Australia.
  2. It is a condition of a development consent for development that involves residential building work for which a contract of insurance is required under the Home Building Act 1989, Part 6 that a contract of insurance is in force before building work authorised to be carried out by the consent commences.
  3. It is a condition of a development consent for a temporary structure used as an entertainment venue that the temporary structure must comply with Part B1 and NSW Part H102 in Volume 1 of the Building Code of Australia.
  4. In subsection (1), a reference to the Building Code of Australia is a reference to the Building Code of Australia as in force on the day on which the application for the construction certificate was made.
  5. In subsection (3), a reference to the Building Code of Australia is a reference to the Building Code of Australia as in force on the day on which the application for development consent was made.
  6. This section does not apply—
    1. to the extent to which an exemption from a provision of the Building Code of Australia or a fire safety standard is in force under the Environmental Planning and Assessment (Development Certification and Fire Safety) Regulation 2021, or
    2. to the erection of a temporary building, other than a temporary structure to which subsection (3) applies.

Condition reason: Prescribed condition under section 69 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021.

2.

Erection of signs 

  1. This section applies to a development consent for development involving building work, subdivision work or demolition work.
  2. It is a condition of the development consent that a sign must be erected in a prominent position on a site on which building work, subdivision work or demolition work is being carried out—
    1. showing the name, address, and telephone number of the principal certifier for the work, and
    2. showing the name of the principal contractor, if any, for the building work and a telephone number on which the principal contractor may be contacted outside working hours, and
    3. stating that unauthorised entry to the work site is prohibited.
  3. The sign must be—
    1. maintained while the building work, subdivision work or demolition work is being carried out, and
    2. removed when the work has been completed.
  4. This section does not apply in relation to - 
    1. building work, subdivision work or demolition work carried out inside an existing building, if the work does not affect the external walls of the building, or
    2. Crown building work certified to comply with the Building Code of Australia under the Act, Part 6.

Condition reason: Prescribed condition under section 70 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021.

3.

Approved plans and supporting documentation 

Development must be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents, except where the conditions of this consent expressly require otherwise.

In the event of any inconsistency with the approved plans and a condition of this consent, the condition prevails.

Condition reason: To ensure all parties are aware of the approved plans and supporting documentation that applies to the development. 

4.

Approved development description 

Consent is granted only to carrying out the development described in detail below:

  • Intensive Livestock Agriculture – Cattle Feedlot to a maximum of 999 Head.

  • Construction of ten (10) feedlot pens and fencing, with each pen measuring no more than 50m x 30m.

  • Construction of a manure pad, sedimentation system, and retention pond.

  • Construction of an internal gravel access road.

  • Construction of upgrades to the existing driveway access point from Ashford Road, subject to Roads Act approval.

Note: Any proposal to modify the terms or conditions of this consent must ensure it remains substantially the same development to that approved, and will require the submission of a formal application under Section 4.55 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 for Council's consideration. In the event that the development will not remain substantially the same, a new application for consent will be required.

Condition reason: To ensure compliance with the development consent. 

5.

Limitation of development approval

This development consent does not approve the proposed 30m x 10m feed shed, proposed silo, or any other infrastructure noted on the site plan which is not listed under condition 4.

All future infrastructure must meet the exempt development provisions of State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008, otherwise further development consent will be required prior to construction or installation.

Condition reason: To ensure compliance with the development consent and reinforce the appropriate approval process for future development.

6.
Prevention of harm and nuisance
The developer shall, in addition to the explicit provisions of this consent, take all reasonable, feasible and practical measures to prevent or minimise harm to the environment and human health during the construction, operation, and where relevant, decommissioning of the development.

Advice: Throughout the life of the development, the person(s) having the benefit of this consent may need to secure, renew, maintain and comply with all the relevant statutory approvals and other legislation applying to the development and ensure that all contractors and subcontractors are aware of, and comply with, the conditions of this consent and other relevant approvals and legislation, including maintaining the necessary insurances. 

The operation of the common law of nuisance runs alongside any statutory obligations under this consent or other legislation. In this respect a precautionary approach should be taken to the operation of the facility, with this consent establishing minimum requirements only.
Condition reason: To ensure that, throughout the life of the development, good practice is exercised with respect to the development.
7.
Compliance with national standards and guidelines - Beef Cattle Feedlots
The feedlot design and ongoing management must comply with the relevant components of the current and any future Meat and Livestock Australia (MLA)Manuals, including:

  • National Guidelines for Beef Cattle Feedlots in Australia (2012) 
  • National Beef Cattle Feedlot Environmental Code of Practice (2012) 
  • Beef Cattle Feedlots Design Manual (2016)
  • Beef Cattle Feedlots: Waste Management and Utilisation (2016).
Condition reason: To ensure that good practice is exercised with respect to the development in perpetuity.
8.
Construction Certificate required
Prior to commencement of any works (including earthworks), a Construction Certificate must be issued in accordance with the Environment Planning and Assessment Act 1979. The application for a Construction Certificate, made to Council or an Accredited Certifier, must include plans and specifications demonstrating full compliance with the Building Code of Australia, associated standards, industry relevant standards, and this consent.
Condition reason: To ensure that the relevant approval is in place to facilitate the necessary certification for the development.


Before issue of a construction certificate

9.
Construction Waste Management
Before the issue of a Construction Certificate, a construction waste management plan must be submitted to and approved by Council. A copy of the approved plan must then be provided to the Accredited Certifier nominating all necessary construction waste management practices and details, including but not limited to the type of waste material and method of disposal, including any temporary storage on site or elsewhere.
Condition reason: To ensure appropriate construction waste management will be undertaken.
10.
Erosion and sediment control plan
Before the issue of a Construction Certificate, an erosion and sediment control plan must be prepared by a suitably qualified person in accordance with the following documents.

  1. The guidelines set out in 'Managing Urban Stormwater: Soils and Construction’ prepared by Landcom (the Blue Book) (as amended from time to time), and 
  2. The ‘Do it Right On-Site, Soil and Water Management for the Construction Industry' (Southern Sydney Regional Organisation of Councils and the Natural Heritage Trust) (as amended from time to time).The plan must be submitted to and approved by Council.  A copy of the approved plan must then be provided to the Accredited Certifier.
Condition reason: To ensure no substance other than rainwater enters the stormwater system and waterways.
11.
Civil works design
Before the issue of a Construction Certificate, the applicant will be required to submit detailed civil engineering designs for the following components of the development:
  • Cut and fill (earthworks);
  • Feed pens and bunkers; and
  • Property access from Ashford Road to demonstrate safe turning paths for access and egress to the property for the maximum design vehicle size. (This is required in addition to the requirement for a Section 138 Roads Act 1993 Approval).
The plan must be submitted to and approved by Council.  A copy of the approved plan must then be provided to the Accredited Certifier.
Condition reason: To ensure that the site civil works are appropriately designed and access is designed to achieve safe and practical traffic movements.
12.
Engineering Design – Hydraulic, Sedimentation and Effluent Storage System
Prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate, the applicant must obtain detailed surveyed engineering drawings, calculations and design documentation for the complete hydraulic and effluent management system for the development. The detailed documentation must be submitted to and approved by Council.  A copy of the approved documentation must then be provided to the Accredited Certifier.

The documentation must be prepared and certified by a suitably qualified and experienced engineer and shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

Hydraulic Design
  1. Catchment areas, runoff coefficients and peak flow calculations for a minimum 20-year ARI design storm.
  2. Detailed plans and hydraulic grade line drawings shall be provided demonstrating the complete flow path of all contaminated runoff from pens, feed aprons, hospital pens, manure stockpiles and trafficable areas through:
    1. collection drains,
    2. sedimentation basins, and
    3. effluent holding ponds,
    4. with no uncontrolled discharge to land or waterways
  3. Cross-sections and longitudinal profiles showing grades, flow depths and velocities.
  4. Flow velocities in drains to exceed 0.5 m/s and remain non-scouring.
Sedimentation System
  1. Detailed design of sedimentation basins demonstrating a maximum internal flow velocity of 0.005 m/s to enable settling of entrained solids prior to discharge to effluent storage.
  2. Basin dimensions, residence time calculations and sediment storage capacity.
  3. Inlet energy dissipation, flow distribution structures, baffles (if proposed), and outlet arrangements to prevent short-circuiting and re-suspension of settled material.
  4. Access and provisions for sediment removal and ongoing maintenance.
Effluent Holding Dam (Retention Pond)
  1. Plans showing the full footprint of the 9.5ML effluent holding dam. Widths, lengths and depths, internal and external batters, and embankment alignments are to be included.
  2. Reduced Levels (RLs) for embankment crest, spillway crest, inlet/outlet structures, top water level and minimum operating level.
  3. Storage capacity calculations including effluent generation, rainfall and evaporation, and a minimum two day emergency storage allowance.
  4. Freeboard for the nominated design storm event.
  5. Liner details (≥300 mm compacted clay or approved synthetic liner, permeability ≤ 0.1 mm/day).
Embankment and Spillway Design
  1. Geotechnical and structural design of embankments including factors of safety for slope stability, seepage, piping and overtopping.
  2. Details of embankment zoning, compaction specifications and construction quality assurance.
  3. Spillway design demonstrating adequate hydraulic capacity for the design storm and erosion protection measures.
  4.  Demonstration that the design minimises the risk of embankment failure and uncontrolled release of effluent.
System Integration
Detailed plans and hydraulic grade line drawings shall be provided demonstrating the complete flow path of all contaminated runoff from pens, feed aprons, hospital pens, manure stockpiles and trafficable areas through:

  1. collection drains,
  2. sedimentation basins, and
  3. effluent holding ponds,
  4. with no uncontrolled discharge to land or waterways.
System Separation
Detailed plans must be provided to demonstrate the location of contour banks constructed upslope and downslope of the feedlot to divert clean stormwater away from operational areas and outside of the sedimentation basin and retention pond.

Consistency with Approved Development
The submitted engineering design shall be generally consistent with the approved development consent and any amended DA plans. Where variations are proposed, an amended development application shall be obtained prior to the issue of the Construction Certificate.
Condition reason: To ensure the hydraulic, sedimentation and effluent storage systems are adequately designed, structurally stable, environmentally compliant, and capable of preventing uncontrolled discharge of effluent in accordance with the National Guidelines for Beef Cattle Feedlots in Australia and the National Beef Cattle Feedlot Environmental Code of Practice.
13.
Section 138 Approval
Before the issue of a Construction Certificate, a separate application must be made to Council for approval under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for:

  • Upgrade works to the existing access crossing.
The application for approval under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 must be accompanied by detailed engineering survey and design.
Condition reason: To ensure all necessary approvals under the Roads Act 1993 are obtained for the development.
14.
Heavy Vehicle Code of Conduct
Before the issue of a Construction Certificate, a Heavy Vehicle Code of Conduct for traffic associated with the feedlot must be submitted to and approved by Council.  The Code of Conduct must address at minimum:
 
  • A map of the primary haulage routes highlighting critical locations;
  • Safety initiatives for haulage through residential areas and/or school zones;
  • An induction process for vehicle operators and regular toolbox meetings;
  • A complaints resolution and disciplinary procedure; and
  • Community consultation measures for peak haulage periods.
A copy of the approved code of conduct must then be provided to the Accredited Certifier.
Condition reason: To promote safe and responsible vehicle use associated with the development.
15.
Comprehensive Operational Plan of Management
Before the issue of a Construction Certificate, a Comprehensive Operational Plan of Management (COPM) must be submitted to and approved by Council. The COPM must address all the relevant details around the day to day operation of the feedlot, including, but not limited to:

  • Standard operating details (days, hours, staffing, pen cleaning schedules, water and effluent monitoring);
  • Effluent management plan which addresses drainage, storage and irrigation in accordance with the NSW Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) Environmental Guidelines: Use of Effluent by Irrigation or other good practice documentation applicable at the time;
  • Biosecurity management, demonstrating compliance with the Biosecurity Act 2015 and Regulation 2016, and any relevant Animal Health Australia guidelines;
  • Heat load management;
  • Operational liquid and solid waste management;
  • Truck, transport and traffic management;
  • Complaints management, including:
    • Installation of signage near the feedlot entrance / end of Ashford Road detailing the operators phone number and email address, for making any complaint;  and
    • Details of the complaints register to be maintained. The register must include at minimum, all responses and any measures taken to address any perceived problems; time and date details; name and contact details of complainants (if known), as well as the climatic conditions on the day of the complaint, those responsible for investigating the complaint; and the resolution of those complaints;
  • Water management; and
  • Hazards (bushfire) management.
A copy of the approved COPM must then be provided to the Accredited Certifier.
Condition reason: To ensure that the comprehensive ongoing management of the feedlot can be undertaken to minimise impact on the built and natural environment.

 

Prior to construction
16.
Erosion and sediment controls in place
Before any site work commences, Council must be satisfied the controls in the erosion and sediment control plan approved under condition 10 are in place. These controls must remain in place until any bare earth has been restabilised in accordance with 'Managing Urban Stormwater: Soils and Construction’ prepared by Landcom (the Blue Book) (as amended from time to time).
Condition reason: To ensure sediment laden runoff and site debris do not impact local stormwater systems and waterways.
17.
Flora and fauna protection
Before any site work commences, the existing Plant Community Types including the trees and associated grass land adjoining the footprint of the feedlot must be protected to prevent any access by construction machinery. Council must be satisfied the measures for tree protection are in place.
Condition reason: To protect and retain trees and grasslands.

During construction
18.
Discovery of relics and Aboriginal objects
While site work is being carried out, if a person reasonably suspects a relic or Aboriginal object is discovered: 

  1. the work in the area of the discovery must cease immediately;
  2. the following must be notified  
    • for a relic – the Heritage Council; or  
    • for an Aboriginal object – the person who is the authority for the protection of Aboriginal objects and Aboriginal places in New South Wales under the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, section 85. 
Site work may recommence at a time confirmed in writing by: 
  1. for a relic – the Heritage Council; or
  2. for an Aboriginal object – the person who is the authority for the protection of Aboriginal objects and Aboriginal places in New South Wales under the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, section 85.
Condition reason: To ensure the protection of objects of potential significance during works.
19.
Implementation of the site management plans
While site work is being carried out:
  • the measures required by the construction site management plan and the erosion and sediment control plan (plans) must be implemented at all times, and
  • a copy of these plans must be kept on site at all times and made available to Council officers upon request.
Condition reason: To ensure site management measures are implemented during the carrying out of site work.
20.
Repair of infrastructure
After completion of all site work:
  1. Any public infrastructure damaged as a result of the carrying out of work approved under this consent (including damage caused by, but not limited to, delivery vehicles, waste collection, contractors, sub-contractors, concreting vehicles) must be fully repaired to the written satisfaction of Council, and at no cost to Council; or
  2. If the works in (a) are not carried out to Council’s satisfaction, Council may carry out the works required and the costs of any such works must be paid as directed by Council and in the first instance will be paid using the security deposit required to be paid under this consent.
Condition reason: To ensure any damage to public infrastructure is rectified.
21.
Construction of drainage infrastructure
During construction, the developer must construct the controlled drainage area to prevent surface water ingress into the feedlot, except during a 1% AEP (1 in 100-year) storm event and to prevent contamination of groundwater.
Condition reason: To manage stormwater effectively and prevent environmental discharge. 
22.
Construction of effluent storage and collection systems
During construction, the effluent storage and collection systems must be constructed and sufficient in capacity to contain all runoff from the controlled drainage area generated in a 1% AEP 24-hour rainfall event.
Condition reason: To prevent potential surface water contamination during major rainfall events.


Before issue of an occupation certificate 

23.

Occupation of premises

Before commencement of the use, an Occupation Certificate must be issued in accordance with Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

Note:  Prior to issue of the Occupation Certificate, the Principal Certifying Authority is required to be satisfied, amongst other things, that:

  • all required inspections (including each applicable mandatory critical stage inspection) have been carried out; and
  • any preconditions to the issue of the certificate required by a development consent have been met.

Condition reason: To ensure an Occupation Certificate is obtained prior to use of the development. 

24.

Commencement compliance inspection

Before commencement of the use, all relevant conditions of this consent must be complied with. To confirm this, an authorised delegate of Council must inspect the development prior to issue of an occupation certificate.

Condition reason: To ensure the proposal has been constructed in accordance with the consent.  

25.
Complaints management
Before commencement of the use, the complaints management protocol forming part of any approved Comprehensive Operational Management Plan must be adopted to the satisfaction of Council.
Condition reason: To ensure that an appropriate complaints management protocol is in place for the feedlot. 

Ongoing use
26.
Ongoing capacity restrictions - water availability
The total number of cattle on the site at any one time must not exceed the maximum herd capacity that can be sustainably supported by the feedlot’s proven, reliable water supply. Accordingly, a report must be provided to Inverell Shire Council each financial year, by 31 July, which addresses:

  • The source of water, including current water licences, for the feedlot site during that financial year;
  • A comparison of the total water available in relation to the maximum feedlot capacity; and
  • In the event of any water restriction and/or water licences are revoked, surrendered, modified, or otherwise removed from the development site:
    • A review of cattle numbers within the feedlot in relation to water supply; and
    • Proposed measures to operate the feedlot to match current water supply (e.g. de-stocking).
Condition reason: To ensure that the feedlot is operated within the capacity of the supporting water supply, in accordance with industry standards, and the development consent to ensure animal welfare is not compromised.
27.
Section 7.11 (94) Contributions
A Sec. 94 (7.11) Contribution for the ongoing maintenance of the local road network is to be paid to Council every quarter, with payments to be made at the following times:

  • Financial quarter January to March – to be paid by 30 May of that year;
  • Financial quarter April to June – to be paid by 31 August of that year;
  • Financial quarter July to September – to be paid by 31 November of that year;
  • Financial quarter October to December – to be paid by 28 February of the next year.

    The current rate is $1.421 per head per quarter and is subject to CPI adjustment each financial quarter.

    The applicant is to provide Council in the month following the end of the financial quarter with details of the cattle head count at the end of the financial quarter. If Council does not receive these details, the contribution will be levied on a maximum processing of 999 head of cattle for that financial quarter.
Condition reason: To ensure that the maintenance from increased traffic movements on the road network are apportionately funded.
28.

Ongoing water monitoring

The operator of the feedlot must undertake visual inspections of the unnamed watercourse located downstream of the development and the Macintyre River to identify any evidence of pollution or environmental harm associated with the operation of the feedlot.

Inspections must be undertaken:
a) At least once in each calendar month while the feedlot is in operation; and
b) Within 24 hours after any overflow event from the retention pond or uncontrolled discharge from the development site.

Inspections must be carried out at the following locations:

  • one point upstream of the development (control point);
  • one point immediately downstream of the development where runoff may enter the unnamed watercourse; and
  • one point within the Macintyre River downstream of the confluence with the unnamed watercourse.

    Each inspection must include observation of indicators such as water discolouration, turbidity, odour, algae growth, or the presence of manure, sediment, foam, oil, or other visible signs of pollution. Photographs must be taken at each monitoring location during every inspection.

    If any evidence of pollution is observed, the operator must immediately take reasonable steps to stop or minimise the source of pollution and notify Council within 24 hours.

    Within seven (7) days of each inspection, the operator must submit a written report to Council including the inspection date and time, inspection locations, observations made, photographic evidence, and details of any actions taken or proposed.

    All monitoring records must be made available to Council upon request.

Condition reason: To ensure the development is operated in a manner that prevents waterway and environmental pollution.

29.

Ongoing effluent management

The effluent structures are to be maintained in good order to prevent failure.The carrying out of the use shall at all times comply with the following requirements: 

  • Effluent may only be applied within the designated Sediment Water Distribution Area (SWDA).

  • Effluent application must not result in surface runoff or spray drift beyond the site boundary.

  • The total quantity of effluent and solid waste applied must not exceed the soil’s ability to absorb nutrient, salt, hydraulic load and organic material. 

For the purposes of this condition, 'effectively utilise' includes the use of the effluent/solids for pasture or crop production, as well as the ability of the soil to absorb the nutrient, salt, hydraulic load and organic material. 

Condition reason: To prevent nutrient build-up and leaching into the subsoil, to guarantee operational control of effluent management, to ensure effluent reuse does not constitute environmental pollution, and to prevent offsite impact from nutrient or spray drift.

30.
Ongoing runoff management
In the event of an uncontrolled release of effluent or runoff, the operator must notify Council immediately and take all reasonable steps to mitigate any environmental harm. 
Condition reason: To ensure appropriate incident response procedures are in place.
31.

Ongoing odour minimisation and management

No offensive odour is to be detected at the nearest sensitive receptor. In the event that odour is detected at the nearest sensitive receptor, the operator is required to take immediate action to identify the odour source and ameliorate the effect.
To ensure odour emissions are effectively minimised, the following operational measures must be implemented for the life of the development:

Pen Management and Manure Control
  1. The feedlot operator must undertake regular pen cleaning to prevent manure build‑up and maintain pen surfaces in a dry, compacted condition.
  2. All manure must be stored within the controlled drainage area and managed using composting methods to reduce odour generation.
  3. Manure pad depth and cleaning schedules must be adjusted in response to seasonal conditions, including rainfall events, humidity, temperature fluctuations and periods of increased moisture risk, to maintain optimum moisture levels that prevent odour formation.
Effluent Pond Management
  1. Effluent ponds must be operated and maintained to avoid the release of offensive odours.
  2. Irrigation of effluent must be carried out using controlled irrigation practices, taking into account environmental conditions, including wind direction/speed, temperature, and atmospheric stability.
  3. Pumping or agitation of effluent ponds must not disturb highly anaerobic effluent layers at the bottom of the pond. Any pumping must be undertaken in a manner that avoids turbulence and minimises odour emissions.
All management practices described in the approved application documents relating to odour reduction (including pen cleaning, manure storage and composting, seasonal moisture control, and effluent pond management) form part of this consent. The development must at all times comply with these measures.

Condition reason: To ensure the development is operated in a manner that prevents offensive odours and protects the amenity of surrounding properties.

32.
Management of asset protection zones (APZ)
A ten (10) metre asset protection zone must be maintained around the feedlot pens and infrastructure in accordance with Planning for Bush Fire Protection 2019.
Condition reason: To ensure ongoing protection from bush fires.

Any other condition deemed appropriate by the Director Environmental Services.


  1. In addition to standards specified in Condition 7, the applicant/developer is to be aware that other separate acts and guidelines are relevant to the carrying out of the use, or an associated activity. These include (but are not limited to):

  • Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1979 and Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Regulation 2025 

  • Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997 and Protection of the Environment Operations (General) Regulation 2022.

  • Local Land Services Act 2013 and Local Land Services Regulation 2014.

  • Biosecurity Act 2015 and Biosecurity Regulation 2016.

  • Work Health and Safety Act 2011.


B. It is recommended the applicant/developer becomes registered under the National Feedlot Accreditation Scheme.


  
AMENDMENT  2026/42
Moved:  Cr John Ross
Seconded:  Cr Wendy Wilks
That:
  1. Council defer consideration of DA-66/2025 to the April 2026 Ordinary Meeting of Council; and
  2. Councillors be provided with a further opportunity to inspect the proposed development prior to further consideration.
The Amendment on being put to the meeting carried. It then became the motion.
The Motion on being put to the meeting was carried.
Carried

Note: Cr Kate Dight left the Chamber at 12:09pm. Cr Williams, Deputy Chair, assumed the Chair.

RESOLUTION  2026/44
Moved:  Cr Greg Kachel
Seconded:  Cr Ian Hooker

That:

  1. Council endorse the trial of a graded (Otta) bitumen seal on a 2.4 kilometre section of the Elsmore Road from the end of the bitumen to Wire Creek Bridge; and
  2. Council allocate funds of $409,000 from the Special Roads Projects program in order to complete the trial.

RESOLUTION  2026/48
Moved:  Cr Wendy Wilks
Seconded:  Cr Fiona Brown

That:

  1. Council confirms with Sports Marketing Australia a commitment to host the 2026 Cricket NSW Country Blitz at a cost of $5,000.00 + GST;
  2. Council funds the management fee of $1,500.00 to Sports Marketing Australia;
  3. Once confirmation is received, Council invoices the Inverell Sports Council as agreed for 50% of the hosting fee, being $2,500.00 + GST;
  4. Council partners with the Inverell Junior Cricket Association and the Inverell Sports Council to deliver the event;
  5. The costs associated with hosting the event be funded from Council's Tourism Industry Promotion Fund; and
  6. The General Manager be authorised to execute the hosting agreement.
Carried

Mr Paul Pay, Director Corporate and Community Services (designated person) declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 12.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay is related to the owners of the land, who are also the proponents of the DA application.

Cr Kate Dight declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 12.5 'Submission - 2026 Murray-Darling Basin Plan Review'. The nature of the interest is that Cr Dight is married to an irrigator in the Border Rivers catchment who has license holdings. 

Cr John Ross declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 12.2 'Proposed Disposal, Planning Proposal and Reclassification - Part Lot 7 DP 1152029, 35 Glen Innes Road, Inverell'.  The nature of the interest is that Cr Ross is the Chairman of the Inverell RSM Club Board.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Mr Justin Pay, Director Civil Services (designated person) declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 12.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay's sister is part owner of the subject property. Please note previous declarations regarding this matter have been made at pre-lodgement stage and submission of DA stage. Mr Pay has taken no part or had no involvement in the assessment of this application. 
  
Mr Paul Pay, Director Corporate and Community Services (designated person) declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 12.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay is related to the owners of the land, who are also the proponents of the DA application. 
  
Cr Greg Kachel declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 12.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'. The nature of the interest is that Cr Kachel has a personal relationship with the owners of the property, to which the DA applies, who are extended family members.

Note: Cr Kachel, Mr Justin Pay and Mr Paul Pay left the Chamber at 10.50 AM.

RESOLUTION  2026/66
Moved:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
Seconded:  Cr Jo Williams

That determination of Development Application 'DA-66/2025 for the Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999-head feedlot and associated infrastructure' at 2321 Ashford Road, Bukkulla be deferred until the 27 May 2026 Ordinary Meeting of Council to facilitate Council obtaining further legal advice in relation to the matter. 
Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr John Ross declared a Non-Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 12.2 'Proposed Disposal, Planning Proposal and Reclassification - Part Lot 7 DP 1152029, 35 Glen Innes Road, Inverell'.  The nature of the interest is that Cr Ross is the Chairman of the Inverell RSM Club Board.

Mr Paul Pay, Director Corporate and Community Services (designated person) declared a Non-Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 12.2 'Proposed Disposal, Planning Proposal and Reclassification - Part Lot 7 DP 1152029, 35 Glen Innes Road, Inverell'. The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay is a Board Member of the Inverell RSM Club Board.

Note: Cr John Ross and Mr Paul Pay left the Chamber at 11:26 AM.

RESOLUTION  2026/71
Moved:  Cr Wendy Wilks
Seconded:  Cr Kelvin Brown

That Council:
  • authorise the General Manager to commence negotiations with Inverell Sporties for the potential sale of the land, based on an independent valuation
  • receive a further report after the receipt of an independent valuation to enable Council to determine an appropriate sale price for the land
  • subject to Inverell Sporties agreeing to the determined sale price, prepare a Planning Proposal to amend the Inverell Local Environmental Plan 2012 to:
  • rezone the land from RE1 Public Recreation to RE2 Private Recreation
  • reclassify the land from Community Land to Operational Land
  • submit the Planning Proposal to the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure for Gateway Determination
  • subject to receipt of a Gateway Determination, undertake public exhibition and conduct a public hearing in accordance with legislative requirements
  • receive a further report following completion of the statutory planning process prior to determining whether to finalise the Planning Proposal and proceed with disposal of the land
  • authorise the affixing of Council’s seal to all necessary documentation.

Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/74
Moved:  Cr Kelvin Brown
Seconded:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
That:

  1. The following works be funded from the Urban Works Vote and be included in the 2026/2027 Budget:

    i. Inverell and Villages - Urban Renewal and Upgrade General Fund, Water Fund

    2. That:
    i. The budget allocations of $3.12M for the 2026/2027 Financial Assistance Grant - Local Road Component Program be endorsed and a further report be presented to Council in respect of the funding allocations and individual works proposed to be undertaken under this program 

    ii. The budget allocation of $160K for the RMS Supplementary Block Grant Program be the subject of a further report to Council

    iii. The budget allocation of $3.22M for the 2026/2027 Block Grant Program be endorsed and a further report be presented to Council in respect of the specific projects to be funded

    iv. The budget allocation of $2.468M for the 2026/2027 Roads to Recovery Program be endorsed and a further report be presented to Council in respect of the specific projects to be funded

    v. The budget allocation of $544.99K for the RERRF/REPAIR Program be endorsed and a report on the projects for the RERRF / REPAIR Program for 2026/2027 be presented to Council in respect of the specific projects to be funded.  

    3. That Council utilises the maximum permissible rate increase allowed by IPART of 3.2%.

    4. That:
    i. Council provide an allocation of $110K for joint industry promotions and assistance

    ii. The 2026/2027 Strategic Capital Infrastructure Fund of $710K be utilised for loan repayments for the Inverell Aquatic Centre Redevelopment

    iii. Additional interest on investments of $446K be allocated to Strategic Capital Infrastructure Fund to fund future capital projects

    iv. The budget allocation of $334K for the 2026/2027 Special Projects - Roads Infrastructure Fund be endorsed

    v. The transfers to and from Internally Restricted Assets be endorsed

    vi. The list of additional one-off budget adjustments listed in section 5.2.2 & 5.2.3 of the report be endorsed.

    5. That:
    i. The following rating categories be utilised for the 2026/2027 rating year:        
           Residential - Inverell
                Residential - General 
                Residential - Ashford
                Residential - Delungra
                Residential - Gilgai
                Residential - Yetman
                Residential - Tingha
                Residential - Rural 
                Business - Inverell Industrial / Commercial 
                Business - Other
                Farmland
                Mining

    ii. A General Base Amount of $242.50 plus an Ad Valorem Rate be determined for the categories detailed above.

    6. That the Interest Rate applicable to Outstanding Rates and Charges for 2026/2027 be the maximum allowable limit as advised by the Office of Local Government. 

    7. That the following Waste Management Charges be adopted:

    8. That the Fees and Charges, as recommended, be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.

    9. That:
    1. the Stormwater Management Service Charge be set at the maximum amount allowable of $25.00 per Residential Premises, $12.50 per Residential Strata lot, and $25.00 for Business Premises for each 350 square metres or additional part thereof, subject to a maximum charge on Business Premises of $200.00
       
    2. the Stormwater Management Service Charge be applied to all land within the Inverell, Ashford, Delungra, Yetman, Gilgai and Tingha urban areas that fall within the residential or business categories for rating purposes (except vacant land)

    3. Council's Revenue Department write to all affected residents and property owners in Tingha to advise them of the proposed charge and provide an opportunity for feedback prior to the adoption of the final rates and charges in June 2026

    4. the Stormwater Management Program as recommended being Gilgai Drainage Project as per the adopted Gilgai Drainage Plan, be adopted 

    10. That the proposed capital expenditure program for 2026/2027 be adopted. 
     
    11. That: 
    i. the report on the 2026/2027 budget be noted

    ii. the draft estimates (incorporating the Operational Plan and Long Term Financial Plan) for the General Fund activities for 2026/2027 be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.

    12. That: 
    1. the Sewerage Charges as listed below be adopted for 2026/2027.


    2. The Draft Estimates (incorporating Operational Plan) for the Sewer Fund for 2026/2027 be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993.

    13. That: 
    1. the Water Charges as listed below be adopted for 2026/2027.



    2. the draft Estimates (incorporating Operational Plan) for the Water Fund for 2026/2027 be adopted and placed on public exhibition for a period of 28 days as required by Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993. 

Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Mr Justin Pay, Director Civil Services (designated person) declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 11.1 and 15.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay's sister is part owner of the subject property. Please note previous declarations regarding this matter have been made at pre-lodgement stage and submission of DA stage. Mr Pay has taken no part or had no involvement in the assessment of this application.

Mr Paul Pay, Director Corporate and Community Services (designated person) declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 11.1 and 15.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay is related to the owners of the land, who are also the proponents of the DA application. 

Cr Greg Kachel declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 11.1 and 15.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.   The nature of the interest is that Cr Kachel has a personal relationship with the owners of the property, to which the DA applies, who are extended family members.

Note: Mr Justin Pay, Mr Paul Pay and Cr Greg Kachel left the Chamber at 11:27 AM.


RESOLUTION  2026/99
Moved:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
Seconded:  Cr Fiona Brown

That determination of Development Application DA-66/2025 for the Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999-head feedlot and associated infrastructure at 2321 Ashford Road, Bukkulla be deferred until a future Ordinary Meeting of Council as the matters detailed within the legal review remain under consideration.
Carried

Note: Cr Fiona Brown left the Chamber at 11:55 AM.

Note: Cr Fiona Brown returned to the Chamber at 11:58 AM.

RESOLUTION  2026/103
Moved:  Cr John Ross
Seconded:  Cr Ian Hooker

That:

  1. Council adopt the amended Stock Grids, Ramps and Gates Policy as attached to the report
  2. Council commence implementation of the Stock Grids, Ramps and Gates Policy and associated licensing framework across the Local Government Area
  3. Existing owners of stock grids, ramps and gates be provided a period of six (6) months from the date of adoption to lodge an application for a Stock Grids, Ramps and Gates Licence
  4.  Licence holders be provided a period of 24 months from the date of adoption to achieve compliance with the requirements of the policy, unless otherwise directed by Council due to safety concerns
  5. Council staff continue to monitor seasonal conditions and the impacts of drought on the rural community during implementation of the policy, with a further report to be presented to Council should consideration of extended implementation timeframes be required
  6. Council staff continue to assess existing stock grids across the Local Government Area to determine licensing status, compliance requirements and where necessary, removal of unlicensed or unsafe structures in accordance with the adopted policy.

Carried
  
Note: Cr Kate Dight returned to the Chamber at 12:17 PM and resumed the Chair.
