RESOLUTION  2026/109
Moved:  Cr Jo Williams
Seconded:  Cr Wendy Wilks

That:
  1. the Report be received and noted
  2. Council make a submission in response to the Emergency Services Funding Reform Options Paper
  3. the following matters be included in the submission
    1. support the principle of broadening emergency services funding across all landowners rather than solely insured property owners
    2. support concession arrangements for pensioners and financially vulnerable property owners
    3. support the proposed concession for vacant land
    4. support the Phased transition arrangement
    5. support Levy Model Option D – Regional Discounts;
    6. advocate for the removal of the current local government contribution towards emergency services funding
    7. advocate for Revenue NSW to administer and collect any replacement levy rather than local government
    8. advocate that, should local government ultimately be required to administer the levy, councils receive an administration fee of no less than 10% to recover the costs associated with implementation and ongoing administration.
    9. ensures that any modelling adopted does not lead to significant increases to current ESLs for farmland 
  4. the draft submission be presented to the Ordinary Meeting of Council to be held on 17 June 2026.

Carried

Mr Paul Pay, Director Corporate and Community Services (designated person), declared a Pecuniary Interest in relation to Item 11.1 and 15.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.  The nature of the interest is that Mr Pay is related to the owners of the land, who are also the proponents of the DA application. 

Cr Greg Kachel declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant Nature in relation to Item 11.1 and 15.1 'DA-66/2025 - Intensive Livestock Agriculture - 999 Head Feedlot and Associated Infrastructure'.   The nature of the interest is that Cr Kachel has a personal relationship with the owners of the property, to which the DA applies, who are extended family members.

    1. Projected capital costs of the development of a FOGO processing model
    2. Projected ongoing costs of the FOGO processing model
    3. The current limited and expected future throughput of food and organic waste streams to the Inverell Landfill and landfills and waste transfer stations within the Shire
    4. The unnecessary financial impost on ratepayers, particularly those in rural (farming areas)
    5. The uncertainty surrounding the viability and positive impact of the FOGO concept.

  3. A copy of Council's representations be provided to the Member for Northern Tablelands Brendan Moylan MP. 
Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/133
Moved:  Cr Wendy Wilks
Seconded:  Cr Jo Williams

That Inverell Shire Council:

  1. Endorse Dr Joe McGirr MP's Rural Health Action Plan as a practical framework for addressing the significant health inequities experienced by rural, regional and remote communities across New South Wales.
  2. Support the six key actions identified within the Rural Health Action Plan, namely:
    a. A GP Guarantee – ensuring every town has access to a doctor through flexible, team-based models of care and the training and retention of a local health workforce.
    b. Birth Closer to Home – improving access to safe, local maternity services through the reopening and enhancement of rural birthing units and expansion of midwife-led and culturally safe models of care.
    c. Local Staff, Not Fly-ins – reducing reliance on costly locum arrangements by redirecting investment towards permanent health professionals, workforce housing and support services.
    d. Local Voices, Real Power – ensuring genuine community consultation and embedding local communities, including First Nations communities, in health governance and decision-making.
    e. A Watchdog for Rural Health – establishing an independent Rural Health Commissioner to provide accountability and oversight of rural health outcomes.
    f. One System, Working Together – improving integration and collaboration between hospitals, general practitioners, community health providers and other health services through Rural Health Precincts and coordinated service delivery.
  3. Endorse the Local Government NSW (LGNSW) 'Caring for our Regions' six-point advocacy campaign, recognising its alignment with the objectives of Dr McGirr's Rural Health Action Plan and its focus on securing equitable access to healthcare services for regional communities.
  4. Write to the Premier of New South Wales, the Minister for Health, the Member for Northern Tablelands, Dr Joe McGirr MP, Local Government NSW and neighbouring councils advising of Council's support for these initiatives and advocating for the implementation of measures that improve healthcare access and outcomes in rural and regional communities.

Carried

  1. That Council adopt the Draft Plan of Management for the Homes for the Aged, Inverell unamended and as presented in accordance with Section 40 of the Local Government Act 1993.

    ii)  Specific lease provisions regarding any intended lease to BEST Employment Ltd.


Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/187
Moved:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
Seconded:  Cr Ian Hooker

That Council provide no financial relief under Council's Water Usage Charges - Undetected Leaks Policy on the basis that:
  • The application does not include a written statement from a licensed plumber, explaining why the leak was not detected or could not have been detected, as required by Clause 9(a) of the Policy. 
  • The applicant has not demonstrated that all reasonable steps were taken to rectify the leak promptly following notification by Council on 16 December 2025, noting that the repair/capping was undertaken in June 2026. 
  • The application was not received within the timeframe prescribed by Clause 9(c) of the Policy. 
  • The available evidence does not support a finding that the leak was undetectable as required by Clause 9(d) of the Policy. 
  • The application does not satisfy all criteria required for financial relief under Council's Water Usage Charges – Undetected Leaks Policy.
Carried

That:

  1. Council note the amendments made to the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 by the Local Government (General) Amendment (Meetings) Regulation 2026.
  2. In accordance with Part 20 of its 2023 Code of Meeting Practice and the relevant provisions of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, establish a Strategy and Policy Committee.
  3. The function of the Strategy and Policy Committee is to review more complex matters considered to be of significant strategic and/or policy importance prior to referral to Council for determination.
  4. The Strategy and Policy Committee consist of all Councillors.
  5. The Strategy and Policy Committee meet on the second Wednesday of every month unless determined otherwise by the Committee or Council.
  6. A review of the effectiveness and performance of the Strategy and Policy Committee take place prior to the adoption of a new Code of Meeting Practice by Council.

Carried

The Committee recommend to Council that:

  1. the report be received and noted.
  2. Council support, in principle, the adoption of a mixed valuation methodology for NSW Local Government, whereby fair value is retained for marketable asset classes and a cost-based approach is adopted for specialised infrastructure assets, subject to an appropriate transition framework.

COMMITTEE RESOLUTION
Moved: Cr John Ross
Seconded: Cr Fiona Brown

The Committee recommend to Council that:
  1. Council establish a Multi-Purpose Indoor Sport and Event Centre Sunset Committee
  2. the Sunset Committee operate in an advisory capacity only, with all recommendations to be referred to Council for consideration and determination
  3. draft Terms of Reference be prepared for consideration by the Sunset Committee and subsequent endorsement by Council
  4. The composition of the Sunset Committee for the feasibility stage of the project be:
    1. the Mayor, as an ex-officio member
    2. the Deputy Mayor
    3. two (2) Councillor representatives
    4. one (1) representative from the Inverell Sports Council (President or their delegate)
    5. the Director Civil Services
  5. The two (2) Councillor representatives on the Sunset Committee be Cr Ian Hooker and Cr Greg Kachel.

RESOLUTION  2026/195
Moved:  Cr Fiona Brown
Seconded:  Cr John Ross

That:
  1. the minutes of the Strategy and Policy Committee Meeting held on Wednesday, 12 August 2026 be received and noted; and
  2. the following recommendations of the Strategy and Policy Committee be adopted by Council. 
10.4.1  Request for Waiver of Hire Fees - Tingha Town Hall - Redeemer Baptist School Ltd - S22.12.1/19
That the request from the Redeemer Baptist School Ltd to have the Tingha Town Hall hire fees waived, be acceded to.
 
10.4.2  2026-2027 Bush Bursary Program - S12.22.1/19

 That:
  
  1. Council participates in the 2026/2027 Bush Bursary Program by co-funding placements at a cost of $3,000 plus GST. This contribution would provide 4 students the opportunity to experience our region for 4 nights (2 nights in the Inverell Shire and 2 nights in a nearby local government area).
  2. Sponsorship be provided depending on the ability of the Inverell Community Health Forum to appoint a representative to liaise with the Rural Doctors Network throughout the process of organising the placement and to undertake all responsibilities of Council.
10.4.3   Bitumen Resurfacing Program 2026-2027 - S28.28.2/18

 That:
  
  1. the proposed 2026-2027 Bitumen Resurfacing Program be adopted as presented
  2. the adopted Bitumen Resurfacing Program for 2026-2027 be placed on Council’s website for the information of the community.
10.4.4   New Residential Areas Drainage Assessment Reports - S18.6.75
 
 That:
  
  1. Council endorse the Draft Drainage Assessment Reports for the three (3) New Residential Areas for public exhibition for a period of 28 days
  2. Council receive a further report following the completion of the public exhibition period should any submissions be received requiring Council's consideration
  3. In the event that no submissions are received during the public exhibition period, Council adopt the Draft Drainage Assessment Reports for the three (3) New Residential Areas as the final Drainage Assessment Reports.
10.4.5  Local Government Asset Valuation - Discussion Paper - S4.2.1
 
 That:
  
  1. the report be received and noted.
  2. Council support, in principle, the adoption of a mixed valuation methodology for NSW Local Government, whereby fair value is retained for marketable asset classes and a cost-based approach is adopted for specialised infrastructure assets, subject to an appropriate transition framework.  
  3. staff prepare a draft Office of Local Government Asset Valuation Methodology Review Feedback Form, reflecting the Committee preferred position and present the Feedback Form to the 26 August 2026 Ordinary Council Meeting for consideration and endorsement prior to lodgement with the Office of Local Government by the closing date of 11 September 2026.
10.4.6  Renewal of Yetman Asbestos Cement Water Mains - S32.13.6
 
 That:
  
  1. the renewal of all asbestos cement water mains within the Yetman water reticulation network be endorsed
  2. funds for the project for the amount of $485,853 come from the Water Fund reserves.
10.4.7   Multi Purpose Indoor Sport and Event Centre Sunset Committee - S4.11.29
 
 That:
  
  1. Council establish a Multi-Purpose Indoor Sport and Event Centre Sunset Committee
  2. the Sunset Committee operate in an advisory capacity only, with all recommendations to be referred to Council for consideration and determination
  3. draft Terms of Reference be prepared for consideration by the Sunset Committee and subsequent endorsement by Council
  4. The composition of the Sunset Committee for the feasibility stage of the project be:

    1. the Mayor, as an ex-officio member
    2. the Deputy Mayor
    3. two (2) Councillor representatives
    4. one (1) representative from the Inverell Sports Council (President or their delegate)
    5. the Director Civil Services

  5. The two (2) Councillor representatives on the Sunset Committee be Cr Ian Hooker and Cr Greg Kachel.
10.4.8   Information Reports
  
  1. Capital Works Update
  1. Outstanding Actions
     
That the information reports be received and noted.
  
Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/191
Moved:  Cr Kate Dight
Seconded:  Cr Jo Williams


That Council:

  1. Welcomes the Federal Government’s recent announcement recognising the very real challenge of financial sustainability impacting the Local Government sector and committing to a meaningful, ongoing, annual increases in the level of Financial Assistance Grants;
  1. Welcomes the announcement of the Federation Compact with Local Government that commits to:
    1. Ongoing annual increases to Financial Assistance Grants to return them to historic levels;
    2. Ensure Roads to Recovery funding can be used to purchase plant and equipment to enable councils to carry out their own road maintenance with their own trained workers, to the extent possible;
    3. Support and increase the availability of apprenticeships in local government, as well as other employment programs in a local government context;
    4. Deliver new capabilities to improve outcomes in housing, planning, emergency management and aged care; and
    5. Ensure the Government publishes an annual summary of funding for Local Government.

  2. Write to the Prime Minister and Local Government Minister Catherine King welcoming their commitment to address the crisis in local government financial sustainability and urging them to work with the local government sector to urgently progress the Federation Compact with Local Government. 

Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/233
Moved:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
Seconded:  Cr Kelvin Brown


That:
  1. there shall be a Deputy Mayoral position on Council
  2. the term of office for this position be for 2 years
  3. In the event that more than one candidate has been nominated for the position of Deputy Mayor, the method of election for Deputy Mayor be determined by Council
  4. The nomination forms and ballot papers used in the election be destroyed following the declaration of the result.

Carried

The Returning Officer advised that a conforming nomination from Cr Joanne Williams had been received. 

Cr Williams had accepted the nomination.

There being only one nomination, the election was dispensed with and Cr Joanne Williams was declared re-elected unopposed as Deputy Mayor for the ensuing two (2) year period.

RESOLUTION  2026/263
Moved:  Cr Jo Williams
Seconded:  Cr Fiona Brown

That:


  1. the report be received and noted.
  2. Council's DRAFT 2025/2026 Financial Statements be "referred to audit" in accordance with s413(1) of the Local Government Act 1993.
  3. if during the audit process, the NSW Audit Office requires any material changes, or discovers any audit issues that would render the Financial Statements false or misleading in any way, the draft financial statements are to be returned to Council for further consideration.
     
  4. Council record as an opinion of Council, in accordance with s413(2c) of the Local Government Act 1993, that the draft 2025/2026 annual financial report is in accordance with:
  • the Local Government Act 1993 (as amended) and the Regulations made thereunder
  • the Australian Accounting Standards and professional pronouncements
  • the Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting
  • presents fairly the Council’s operating result and financial position for the year
  • accords with Council’s accounting and other records
  • that the Council is not aware of any matter that would render this report false or misleading in any way..
  1. subject to no material audit changes or audit issues discovered as a result of the audit process:
  1. the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, General Manager and Responsible Accounting Officer be authorised to sign the statements as required by s413(2) of the Local Government Act 1993
  1. Council authorise the General Manager to forward the Financial Statements to the Office of Local Government upon receipt of the Audit Reports from the NSW Audit Office
  1. Council authorise the General Manager to place the audited Financial Statements on public exhibition and provide notice in accordance with s418(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, that Council will consider the Reports of its Auditors for the year ended 30 June 2026 at its November Ordinary Meeting
  1. Council present the signed audited Financial Statements to the public at the November Ordinary Council Meeting in accordance with s419(1) Local Government Act 1993.



Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/236
Moved:  Cr John Ross
Seconded:  Cr Greg Kachel

  1. That the minutes of the Waste Management Sunset Committee Meeting held on 19 August 2026 be received and noted
  2. the following recommendations of the Waste Management Committee be adopted by Council. 
10.1.1 Consideration of Education and Community Engagement Requirements
 
That:
  1. The report be received and noted
  2. Preliminary community communication commence to inform residents of the NSW Government's Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) mandate and Council's ongoing investigations and planning activities associated with the future implementation of the service
  3. A Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) Education and Communication Plan be developed, including consideration of the NSW Environment Protection Authority's Scrap Together program and associated educational resources
  4. A further report be presented to Council outlining the proposed FOGO implementation program, community engagement strategy and service delivery model following completion of Council's ongoing investigations and planning activities.
 
10.1.2 Draft Waste and Resource Recovery Strategy 2027-2036 - Progress Update
 
That:
  1. The report be received and noted
  2. Committee members be invited to review the Draft Waste and Resource Recovery Strategy 2027–2036 and provide any comments or feedback to Council's Director Environmental Services for consideration prior to the preparation of a report to Council
  3. A further report be presented to Council seeking endorsement of the Draft Waste and Resource Recovery Strategy 2027–2036 for public exhibition.
 
10.1.3 Information Reports
 
  • NSW Battery Project Stewardship Scheme
  • Update on Waste Management Activities
That the information reports be received and noted.
 


10.1.4 Food Organics and Garden Organics Collection Service Delivery Options
 
That:
  1. The report be received and noted
  2. It be noted that the report identifies a custom exemption, based on the lot size provisions of the Inverell Local Environmental Plan 2012, as the preferred service delivery model should Council's application for an indefinite exemption from the NSW Environment Protection Authority (EPA) be unsuccessful
  3. A further report be prepared following receipt of the NSW Environment Protection Authority's determination of Council's application for an indefinite exemption from the NSW Government's Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) mandate
  4. The preliminary response received from the NSW Environment Protection Authority seeking additional information to enable the determination of Council's request for a Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) mandate exemption be noted. 
 
Carried

RESOLUTION  2026/237
Moved:  Cr Wendy Wilks
Seconded:  Cr Fiona Brown


That:
  1. the minutes of the Strategy and Policy Committee Meeting held on Wednesday, 9 September 2026 be received and noted
  2. the following recommendations of the Strategy and Policy Committee be adopted by Council.

10.2.1 Re-Nomination of Council Representatives to the Northern Regional Planning Panel
 
That Mrs Dianna Baker and Mr Brett McInnes, General Manager be re-nominated as Council representatives to the Northern Regional Planning Panel for a term of three (3) years.
  

10.2.2 2026 Business Retention and Expansion Survey  

That:

  1. The report be received and noted
  2. Council utilise the data collected to assist in reviewing the Inverell Shire Community Strategic Plan, inform future strategic direction, guide economic development priorities and identify key issues requiring advocacy on behalf of the business community. 
  
10.2.3 Local Government Performance Ratios Discussion Paper S4.2.1  

That:

  1. the report be received and noted
  2. staff prepare a draft Office of Local Government Performance Ratios Feedback Form, and present the Feedback Form to the Ordinary Council Meeting on 23 September 2026 for consideration and endorsement prior to lodgement with the Office of Local Government by the closing date of 7 October 2026.
  
10.2.4 Gravel Resheeting Program 2026-27 S28.21.1/19  

That: 

  1. the 2026-2027 Gravel Resheeting Program as presented be adopted
  2. the program be placed on Council’s website for the information of the community.
  
10.2.5 Inverell Taxi Rank Refurbishment - Funding Allocation S28.7.29  

That:
 
  1. The final engineering, architectural and artwork plans for the refurbishment of the Inverell Taxi Rank in Vivian Street, for the purpose of construction be approved at tender construction stage.
  2. Council allocate $490,503 excluding GST from the 2026/2027 Budget for the Inverell Taxi Rank Refurbishment Project, $300,000 from the 2025/2026 Taxi Rank Budget allocation and $190,503 from the 2026/2027 Strategic Capital Infrastructure Fund.
  3. Council authorise the General Manager to finalise the tender documentation and undertake the procurement process for the construction of the project.
 
10.2.6 Information Reports

  • Outstanding Actions Registry
  • Capital Works Update
  
That the information reports be received and noted.  

10.2.7 Award Tender - Inverell Sporting Complex Netball Courts Upgrade S5.9.38  

That:

  1. Council reduce the scope of the tender by removing demolition of existing courts and initial pavement works from the awarded project.
  2. Council undertake the demolition, earthworks and initial pavement works for the project.
  3. Council accept the tender from Conseth Solutions of $1,461,958.23.
  4. Council allocate additional funds of $217,632 to the project from Council’s 2026/2027 Strategic Capital Infrastructure Fund.
  5. The General Manager be delegated authority to execute the finalised contract with Conseth Solutions.

Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr John Ross declared a Non Pecuniary Interest of a Significant nature in relation to Item 11.7 'Proposed Disposal, Planning Proposal and Reclassification - Part Lot 7 DP 1152029, 35 Glen Innes Road, Inverell - Proposed Sale Price'. The nature of the interest is that Cr Ross is Chairperson of the Board of Directors of the Inverell RSM Club.  

Note: Cr John Ross left the Chamber at 10:54 AM.

RESOLUTION  2026/252
Moved:  Cr Paul King (OAM)
Seconded:  Cr Wendy Wilks

That Council:

  1. determine the sale price for the approximately 4,000 square metre portion of Part Lot 7 DP 1152029 adjoining Inverell Sporties at $50,000 exclusive of GST.
  2. note that Inverell Sporties have indicated agreement to the proposed sale price of $50,000 exclusive of GST.
  3. proceed with the preparation of a Planning Proposal to amend the Inverell Local Environmental Plan 2012 to:
    1. rezone the land from RE1 Public Recreation to RE2 Private Recreation and
    2. reclassify the land from Community Land to Operational Land.
  4. submit the Planning Proposal to the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure for Gateway Determination.
  5. subject to receipt of a Gateway Determination, undertake public exhibition and conduct a public hearing in accordance with legislative requirements.
  6. require Inverell Sporties to meet all costs associated with the Development Application, any required third-party environmental or technical studies, subdivision survey and registration of the subdivision with NSW Land Registry Services.
  7. fund the internal costs associated with the preparation and processing of the Planning Proposal, rezoning and reclassification of the land, including the cost of the required public hearing.
  8. receive a further report following completion of the statutory planning process prior to determining whether to finalise the Planning Proposal and proceed with disposal of the land.

RESOLUTION  
Moved:  Cr Fiona Brown
Seconded:  Cr Jo Williams

The Committee recommend that Council:

  1. Note the release of the Local Government NSW and Water Directorate Action Plan, Securing Our Water Supply: Delivering safe, reliable and affordable water and sewerage services for regional communities at risk.
  2. Endorse the proposed action plan, which calls on the NSW Government to:
    • Provide capital grant funding of $5 billion for at least a further 10 years.
    • Strengthen drinking water quality in rural, regional and remote NSW including support for Local Water Utilities to address emerging contaminants such as PFAS.
    • Reduce unnecessary regulatory burdens on Local Water Utilities in rural, regional and remote NSW including the NSW Regulatory and Assurance Framework, water utility strategic planning and Section 60 approvals.
    • Implement a complementary Community Service Obligation model for better targeted, more efficient and predictable funding for councils that cannot raise sufficient revenue to meet the costs of running their water and sewerage systems.
    • Commit $4 million per annum to a Local Water Utilities Alliance program, enabling utilities to share expertise, access specialist skills, coordinate planning and to respond more effectively to droughts, emergencies and asset management challenges.
    • Commit to a $15 million, 10 year Regional Water Workforce Development Program to build a skilled and sustainable regional water workforce and allocate $2.5 million over 5 years to create dedicated career pathways for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
  3. Write to the Premier and Minister for Water:
    • Asking that the NSW Government adopt the Securing Our Water Supply Action Plan.
    • Setting out the risks for Council’s water and sewer services if the NSW Government fails to take action.
Carried
